quick: No initial adjustment; caution if severe
Start low; max 40 mg in mild-moderate
summary: Telmisartan is a long-acting angiotensin II receptor blocker used to treat hypertension and reduce cardiovascular risk in patients intolerant of ACE inhibitors. Dosed 40-80 mg once daily. Contraindicated in pregnancy; monitor potassium and renal function.
indications: Treatment of hypertension to lower blood pressure
Cardiovascular risk reduction in patients >=55 years at high CV risk unable to take ACE inhibitors

dosage.d: Consider lower starting dose under supervision

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Do not remove tablet from blister until immediately before dosing
Correct volume/salt depletion before starting if present
Take at the same time each day
Monitor BP, electrolytes and renal function periodically
moa: Selectively and durably blocks the angiotensin II type-1 (AT1) receptor, preventing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone secretion. This lowers peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure without affecting bradykinin (hence less cough than ACE inhibitors).

absolute: Concomitant aliskiren in patients with diabetes
monitor: Combination with ACE inhibitor or aliskiren

preg: Contraindicated. Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal injury and death, especially in the second and third trimesters. Discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected.
lact: Not recommended; no data on excretion in human milk. Consider alternative agent or discontinue nursing.
renal: No initial dose adjustment needed, including dialysis patients. Use caution and monitor renal function in severe impairment or renal artery stenosis; not removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: Largely eliminated in bile; use with caution. In mild-to-moderate impairment do not exceed 40 mg once daily. Contraindicated in biliary obstructive disorders and severe hepatic impairment.

major: ACE inhibitors - avoid dual RAAS blockade (renal failure, hyperkalemia, hypotension)
moderate: NSAIDs - reduced antihypertensive effect and acute renal failure (especially elderly/volume-depleted)
Lithium - increased lithium levels and toxicity
interactions.alcohol: May potentiate hypotensive effect; advise caution.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum potassium and creatinine.

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and follow-up
Serum potassium, particularly with diuretics/renal disease
Renal function (creatinine, BUN) after initiation and dose changes
Volume status in patients on diuretics
counsel: Take once daily, with or without food, at the same time
Rise slowly to reduce dizziness; report fainting
Avoid potassium supplements/salt substitutes unless advised
Stop and contact provider immediately if pregnant
pk: Antihypertensive effect within 3 hours; apparent by 2 weeks
Store at 20-25 C; keep in blister until use
pearls: Longest half-life among ARBs - strong 24-hour BP control
Useful CV protection alternative when ACE inhibitor not tolerated
Avoid dual RAAS blockade - no benefit, more harm
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it; do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Most likely manifestation is hypotension and tachycardia (or bradycardia). Treat supportively with IV fluids and supine positioning. Telmisartan is not removed by hemodialysis.
